ai.name: Ox Alpha (mystery model)
ai.hook: A mystery coding model appears, likely a hidden **Zhipu/GLM** release beating expectations without a bigger base.
insights: Analysts trace gains to **post-training and infra**, not raw parameter scale, built on GLM-5.2's 743B base
Uses a technique called **SAO** for long-horizon agentic tasks
Chinese labs are now competing on price/performance and multimodal agents, not just size
ai.for_you: This is the trend underpinning your whole agency thesis: capable models are getting cheap enough to route SMB clients through open/Chinese models instead of paying OpenAI/Anthropic prices.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Clearest signal today of the open-model cost curve bending, directly relevant to margin on client work

ai.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
ai.hook: DeepSeek ships a multimodal model that performs near Opus-4.8 at a fraction of the assumed cost.
insights: Performance benchmarks land close to Anthropic's Opus-4.8 tier
Part of a broader pattern of Chinese labs pressuring US pricing on capability-per-dollar
ai.for_you: Worth a quick eval this week: swap your agency's vision/OCR tasks (invoice reading, doc parsing for PT SMB clients) onto this via OpenRouter and compare cost vs GPT-4o-class pricing.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete new release with direct cost implications for client-facing multimodal work

ai.name: AT&T open-model routing
ai.hook: AT&T routes 40% of employee AI usage to open models, aiming for 60-70%, cutting coding costs 56%.
insights: Only a **2% quality drop** at 45 billion tokens/day of traffic
Signals enterprise-grade hybrid routing (closed for hard tasks, open for volume) is now proven at scale
Reinforces the OpenRouter/Stripe deal logic: routing infrastructure is where the margin sits
ai.for_you: This is the exact architecture to pitch PT SMB clients: route routine tasks (support replies, content drafts) to cheap open models, reserve frontier models for edge cases, and bill the savings as your value-add.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Real enterprise proof point for a hybrid routing pitch, not just a lab announcement

ai.name: Ornith-1.5
ai.hook: New MIT-licensed open model family ships in 9B, 35B MoE, and 397B MoE sizes with built-in self-improvement.
insights: Quantized formats include **FP8, GGUF, MLX, NVFP4**
Qwen3.8-27B GGUFs with Dynamic V3 quantization hit **10% higher accuracy**
1-bit quantization retains 77% of BF16 accuracy while running on just **8GB RAM**
ai.for_you: The 9B or 35B MoE variant is small enough to self-host for a client demo, useful if you want to offer an on-prem/data-sovereign pitch to PT SMBs wary of sending data to US clouds.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only genuinely new open-weight release with a usable small-size variant this week

ai.name: Nvidia's fishing-not-fish strategy
ai.hook: Nvidia is pushing companies to train their own models instead of just buying tokens from Anthropic/OpenAI.
insights: Framed as 'teaching everyone to fish' rather than selling fish (inference)
Part of Nvidia's push to keep GPU demand tied to training, not just serving
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, worth revisiting if you ever consider fine-tuning your own small model for the yoga platform's content generation.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Best framing today of the infra-vs-model-buying tension shaping AI economics

ai.name: Matt Webb on learning with ChatGPT
ai.hook: Learning quaternions via ChatGPT as a patient tutor pushed him to learn more, not less.
insights: He didn't ask ChatGPT to write code, he asked it to **teach him** the math first
Outsourcing thinking to AI didn't stop learning, it redirected effort toward deeper understanding
ai.for_you: This is your actual learning path for technical fluency: use models as tutors for the concepts blocking your build (auth flows, vector DBs, API design) instead of just generating code you don't understand.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most practical mindset shift for a non-developer PM learning to build

ai.name: Simile / Joon Sung Park
ai.hook: Digital twins now reproduce human behavior with 85% accuracy of people reproducing their own answers.
insights: Built via long-form interviews plus observational, transaction, and RCT data, not just prompting
Requires changing model weights, not just prompt engineering, to capture irrational human behavior
Ambition: simulate products and policies on population-scale digital twins before shipping
ai.for_you: Conceptually interesting for testing yoga platform messaging or pricing on simulated personas before running real ad spend, but the tech isn't accessible at your scale yet, filed for awareness only.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive podcast release this week with a genuinely novel research direction

build_this.name: n8n
build_this.what_it_is: Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities, 400+ integrations, self-host or cloud.
build_this.why_try_it: Directly usable for your AI agency: build a client-facing automation (lead intake to WhatsApp/email response to CRM update) this week as a productized offer for a PT SMB, self-hosted so you control cost and data.

build_this.name: Claudette (nobuzz)
build_this.what_it_is: A small tool/prompt set that stops Claude from writing like a BuzzFeed article.
build_this.why_try_it: Steal this pattern for the yoga platform's content generation, apply it as a system prompt layer so AI-drafted meditation copy doesn't sound like generic listicle filler.

build_this.name: Shoehorn
build_this.what_it_is: Quantizes any model down to run on your own machine.
build_this.why_try_it: Quick experiment this week: quantize a small open model (like Ornith-1.5's 9B variant) to run locally, useful if you want to demo a data-sovereign, offline AI feature to a PT SMB client worried about cloud data leaving the country.
